reusable_fixture.caveat: Packet was saved by the later FP32 reproduction, not the original Stage B BF16 command. Its tokens/cotangent match original hashes and FP32 reproduced all 101 historical tensor metrics; historical BF16 outputs/gradients were not saved.

precision_localization_hypotheses: Historical tiled atts/sum_scores and k_grads/v_grads allocate using x.dtype. The new actual-CE trace observes atts/sum_scores AND running max_logit FP32 at helper boundaries. It observes cached projection inputs as BF16; gs/g_dot_atts remain source-only projection-dtype inferences in this legacy trace.
block_attention_add computes logits/exponentials/weighted sum before adding to high-precision state; FP32 destination does not recover rounded source intermediates.
recompute_alphas explicitly softmaxes in FP32 then casts to q.dtype. recompute_atts consumes those low-precision alphas. Temporal formulas mutate alphas and build q gradients from these tensors.
Naive uses full causal-prefix softmax; tiled uses online accumulation then distinct backward recomputation. They need separately explicit policies; neither BF16 backend is automatically an oracle.

Backend-gradient differences concentrate around block3 but common-reference failures occur throughout the model. End-to-end records alone cannot attribute a faulty operation or distinguish acceptable BF16 roundoff from a correctable precision-policy defect.

cpu_api_inspection.custom_fwd_signature: (fwd=None, *, device_type: str, cast_inputs: torch.dtype | None = None)
cpu_api_inspection.interpretation: Installed custom_fwd with cast_inputs non-None casts floating inputs and disables autocast internally; default None preserves current state. custom_bwd restores the forward autocast state. Neither decorator by itself enforces FP32 sensitive recurrent reductions.

candidate_core_read_only_review.policy: recurrent_precision_policy=bf16_fp32_state; inactive outside CUDA BF16 autocast; active branch requires FP32 residual input.
checked: Naive one-time FP32 Q/K/V views remain graph-connected and shared across temporal attention uses; no detach breaks the projection gradient.
Tiled forward retains BF16 storage for K/V and separate FP32 attention arithmetic; backward distinguishes saved forward projection/autocast dtype from promoted arithmetic Q dtype.
Detached tiled recomputation values are accompanied by graph-connected FP32 Q/K/V projection views receiving the manually accumulated adjoints once.
Attention is cast back to BF16 before forward output projection, per-token MLP recomputation, and batched MLP parameter-gradient recomputation.
Sensitive helper arithmetic explicitly disables autocast and promotes operands in the selected branch; manual backward runs with autocast disabled except the dense recomputation sections.

Legacy/FP32 arithmetic retains its original casts and expressions through inactive branches. No parameters, tensor ownership, state_dict keys, rho equations, masks, or norm implementation were changed.
limits: Read-only review establishes no numerical or training clearance. Helper signatures/compiled code changed, so exact historical FP32 regression remains a runtime gate.
No claim that all residual BF16 discrepancy is fixed; rounded dense projections and attention cast boundaries remain intentionally BF16.
The policy also requires the declared TF32-off runtime profile; FP32 tensor dtype alone does not guarantee IEEE FP32 matmul when external backend flags differ.
candidate_core_read_only_review.integration_caveat: convert_model rejects cross-policy conversion by default because the new config field is outside its allowed-difference set. Current validation/operational harnesses load authoritative state dicts directly, so this is not a blocker. Keep fail-closed behavior unless explicit cross-policy weights-only conversion is intended.
